Bakir.statement: But the boyaress's blood guards are running unchecked. And Bakir is in the dungeons.

Bakir.speaker: 90B50BB544F2B7AAA12E95A77975B34F
Bakir.statement: Well, with Ambrus and Bakir dead, the regular forces are in dissaray.

Bakir.speaker: 40B6CBC3412EB87CCA40ED9C4E2A5229
Bakir.statement: Bakir was thorough, I'll grant him that...

Bakir.speaker: AC954D7F467554FFED9FADB26DC9C52D
Bakir.statement: But... they didn't know that we'd been planning our escape since Bakir had given up the ghost.

Bakir.speaker: FF66F1954A6F18E4728CDCB46EE4C113
Bakir.statement: I need to find my family. And you're free because of me. I'm the one that killed Bakir.

Bakir.speaker: 2DF1E0F94C039F44CEA12281930B1222
Bakir.statement: I need to kill Brencis. And you're free because of me. I'm the one that killed Bakir.

Bakir.speaker: 806E3C67469C949ABECBE28B829DF714
Bakir.statement: But I hate him. And I hated Bakir! I'm glad you killed him! I swear!

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: I'm sorry, Farkas, but I have changed my mind. I'm not ready to face Bakir yet.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: You weren't telling me the whole truth, Farkas. Bakir told me about your brother.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: Ah, I see. You’re one of Bakir’s men.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: Honestly, I can even be a flying pig if it allows me to slay Bakir.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: It won’t be easy, Farkas. I doubt I'll just run into Bakir, kill him and then piss off into the sunset.

Bakir.speaker: SQ710.Farkas
Bakir.statement: Just be forewarned – Bakir will keep calling you and the other contestants vermin. You'll need to keep a cool head...

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: Killing Bakir won’t be as simple as you make it sound.

Bakir.speaker: SQ710.Farkas
Bakir.statement: Trust me or not, I’m your best chance at getting rid of Bakir.

Bakir.speaker: SQ710.Farkas
Bakir.statement: I know everything Boyar does, and he’s very vocal about the 'vermin-loving traitor from Laslea'. If you want to fool Bakir, you’d better tread carefully.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: I was meant to kill Bakir, not rob him.

Bakir.speaker: SQ710.Farkas
Bakir.statement: It isn't. But if you want to fool Bakir, you’d better tread carefully.

Bakir.speaker: SQ710.Farkas
Bakir.statement: Remember, nothing's too outrageous for Boyar Bakir. He revels in both abuse and affection, humiliation and kindness. To his mind, we are all lesser beings - pests to toy with.

Bakir.speaker: SQ710.Farkas
Bakir.statement: Well, I have reasons for both serving Bakir and wishing him dead.

Bakir.speaker: SQ710.Farkas
Bakir.statement: You see, when the challenge is over, Boyar Bakir takes the champion to the treasury to personally grant them a reward of their own choosing.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: I have a better chance against Bakir than you.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: I have the better chance against Bakir. Believe me.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: If you help me kill Bakir, we could take his entire treasury. Not just a single item from it.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: Prove you're not all bark, and defeat Bakir himself. You will get the whole treasury instead of settling for one meagre piece.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: We could kill Bakir and take his whole treasury.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: If I spare you, you'll just end up as Bakir’s next meal.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: Bakir won't be around to do anything.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: Drop the act, Bakir. Nobody's that insane.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: I haven't invited you yet, Bakir. Not sure if I want your mad whispering in my ear.

Bakir.speaker: SQ710.Farkas
Bakir.statement: God, no! I could never... Bakir took him, the same way he took everything from me – by force.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: Not so fast. Bakir told me about your brother.

Bakir.speaker: SQ710.Farkas
Bakir.statement: You were set on killing Bakir, and I was after the ring. Bringing Dusan into it would only have complicated matters.

Bakir.speaker: SQ710.Farkas
Bakir.statement: But when the vrakhiri came, we ran like mice. My father, my mother, my cousins - Bakir killed them all. Tore their heads off and drank the gushing blood.

Bakir.speaker: SQ710.Farkas
Bakir.statement: Dusko... He was so scared of that bastard. Kept flinching, sobbing... Making himself look 'ugly', Bakir claimed. So he taught my poor brother a lesson... in obedience.

Bakir.speaker: SQ710.Farkas
Bakir.statement: That's why I need the ring. The magic in it... Bakir said it works miracles. Promised he'd give it to me one day, if I managed to amuse him.

Bakir.speaker: SQ710.Sever
Bakir.statement: I thought I was Bakir’s favourite. But one slip-up – one bloody slip-up – and I was on my knees with an apple stuffed in my mouth like some sacrificial pig.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: Bakir lied to you. The ring has nothing to do with healing of any kind. Whatever it contained – it was lethal.

Bakir.speaker: Coen
Bakir.statement: Bakir's gone. So stop listening to him.

Florin.speaker: brencis_soldier.male05
Florin.statement: This Father Florin... he seems like he's hiding something.

Florin.speaker: cc.SideGate.Gossiper.1
Florin.statement: I think Father Florin is the rebel leader.

Florin.speaker: cc.SideGate.Gossiper.2
Florin.statement: They say Father Florin started having opinions of his own. And that's why he's gone now.

Florin.speaker: Coen
Florin.statement: Father Florin.

Florin.speaker: Coen
Florin.statement: I understand, Father Florin.

Florin.speaker: Coen
Florin.statement: I understand, Father Florin. In this fight, we must use every tool at hand.

Florin.speaker: Coen
Florin.statement: You always have an excuse for your actions, Father Florin. But I'm done listening to them.

Florin.speaker: Coen
Florin.statement: Jude the Apostle... I thought Father Florin was supposed to destroy this.

Florin.speaker: q102.believer5
Florin.statement: Huh. Good luck with that. The man is close with Father Florin.

Florin.speaker: q102.guard_without_xanthe8
Florin.statement: Have some respect. He's a good man, that Father Florin.

Florin.speaker: q102.Craftsman
Florin.statement: It's not for me to judge. Father Florin ordered me to make it, so make it I will.

Florin.speaker: q102.Servant
Florin.statement: Now, that's the treasury. Only Father Florin is allowed in. No exceptions!

Florin.speaker: 6947BF1A46C8BA6BF77198B2D0A44947
Florin.statement: After Florin's death, the Church canonised him – he's patron saint of the virtuous. A stinging irony.

Florin.speaker: 2A155C47403F6828AAE82FBBD4F1DFC9
Florin.statement: As soon as Brencis was dethroned, most of Father Florin's flock turned against him - and those still loyal to the priest couldn't protect him.

Florin.speaker: 8381B3184C6DAE5157D9C9876BCD0A5B
Florin.statement: Evil men rarely get what they deserve. I'm glad Florin was an exception.

Florin.speaker: 6BCF1C434D7259F0B13C64B3EE97E8DA
Florin.statement: Father Florin always enjoyed being the centre of attention.

Florin.speaker: D281804842F516A92EEEF5B4D66D7B31
Florin.statement: Having learned of Florin's betrayal, Brencis showed little mercy. He was so offended he even refused to drink the fallen priest's blood.

Florin.speaker: ACFE9EE6439EA6F88C1307B792D32267
Florin.statement: One of the first orders Catalin issued as the newly installed knyaz of Vale Sangora was to burn Florin at the stake.

Florin.speaker: sq712_beggar
Florin.statement: Yeah, he will. For Father Florin's sake - kill him!

Florin.speaker: sq712_christian_1
Florin.statement: No! Father Florin!

Florin.speaker: Coen
Florin.statement: No, Father Florin. I won't help you.

Florin.speaker: Coen
Florin.statement: No. Enough of your sermons. You deserve to die, Father Florin.

Florin.speaker: Coen
Florin.statement: I've been in that building - it's where Father Florin met with his Christians.

Florin.speaker: Coen
Florin.statement: One of the buildings on the map is circled... That's the place Father Florin told me about.

Florin.speaker: Coen
Florin.statement: Seems like Father Florin and his followers are up to something shady...

Florin.speaker: Coen
Florin.statement: So this is where Father Florin made his plans.

Florin.speaker: Coen
Florin.statement: A symbol of a hand. Just like the one I saw in Father Florin's hideout.

Florin.speaker: Coen
Florin.statement: That must be the building from Father Florin's map...

Florin.speaker: Coen
Florin.statement: That's the building Father Florin told me about...

Florin.speaker: sq712_beggar
Florin.statement: It's good that you came. Father Florin says that you might be of great help to us.

Florin.speaker: sq712_guard_2
Florin.statement: Father Florin expects you.

Florin.speaker: Coen
Florin.statement: So one of Father Florin's people was able to brave this maze after all.

Florin.speaker: Coen
Florin.statement: This must be what Father Florin wanted. Now to return to him.

Florin.speaker: sq712_christian_1
Florin.statement: Avenge Father Florin!

Florin.speaker: sq712_christian_3
Florin.statement: I don't know. But if she was... May God and all His saints protect us and Father Florin.

Florin.speaker: sq712_christian_1
Florin.statement: They just tried to do their duty to Father Florin. And you cut them down.

Florin.speaker: sq712_christian_8
Florin.statement: Father Florin says so. And I believe him.

Florin.speaker: sq712_christian_6
Florin.statement: Father Florin trusts you. I suppose that's good enough for me.

Florin.speaker: sq712_christian_8
Florin.statement: Oh, it's you... Please, trust in Father Florin as we do!

Florin.speaker: SQ719.Monk
Florin.statement: Unlike Father Florin, our abbot, Bartalan, was a man of deep faith - so he tried protesting. 'You can't be serious!', he said, 'This is blasphemy!'.

Marat.speaker: Ambrus
Marat.statement: Good fighter, this Marat. Not as good as me, of course...

Marat.speaker: 7FA1521B44DA436BE68BBFBE7BABE5A9
Marat.statement: Keep an eye on Marat for me.

Marat.speaker: 43B9DE5B420F30227DA25196E908EAD0
Marat.statement: My real name is Marat... if you prefer it to Crake.

Marat.speaker: 088AF00B4D09B86E596C36885A127DDE
Marat.statement: Marat was important to me.

Marat.speaker: Coen
Marat.statement: Marat was important to me.

Marat.speaker: 9062497641012EC8F8E2CD85B573704C
Marat.statement: They better be here, Marat. They have to be alive.

Marat.speaker: 87729C104338D2CDF446EFA58D5E37E6
Marat.statement: I remember you. One of Marat's men.

Marat.speaker: ADB5E5C04CAAE210ECCC0BB027D38F0F
Marat.statement: I'm the reason Marat died.

Marat.speaker: 0A291D4845E4CD8B88EC82901756A7F0
Marat.statement: I... I was there. When Marat died. Saw it with my own eyes.

Marat.speaker: 00855031422B04E4A0A721B724D372E2
Marat.statement: Marat... he died because of me.

Marat.speaker: 4B45FD644006BBE055FACBB18E409DA7
Marat.statement: You say Marat failed you... but you've got it the other way round. You didn't deserve him.

Marat.speaker: 6C4B52C942105794DC8644AEDEE0C4BF
Marat.statement: You should know that Marat died a true hero. Fighting for all of Vale Sangora.

Marat.speaker: 9D1008684F23360C2660B4BEFCD9EEA1
Marat.statement: Coen! Yeah, Crake – sorry, Marat – said that he wanted to see Laslea, help [cough] help out with the rebuilding.

Marat.speaker: 6A54D1714CC20CAF42715F87BC642671
Marat.statement: But Marat and the manumits were there to greet them.

Marat.speaker: E18565234BDC324BC6939896B9969704
Marat.statement: Catalin was determined to stamp out all monsters from the valley. And, with Marat's help, he succeeded.

Marat.speaker: 5577F90E4827C52F443F5CA1BC8ADBF5
Marat.statement: Marat and I shared a goal and I grew to respect him. But we never became truly close... I'm not sure he even wanted any friends.

Marat.speaker: EA5EFEDA4A35268C69281DA5C19CDAD0
Marat.statement: Marat got what he wanted – he became Catalin's right hand man. And as such, he enforced his policies with ruthless efficiency...

Marat.speaker: 6184358D440C52B93505A98F5B30D471
Marat.statement: Marat took up his sword to fight against monsters. But as soon as they were gone, he learned that humans could be just as cruel and bloodthirsty.

Marat.speaker: F5CEBD374C5A96BE5626DC955B4091C7
Marat.statement: Marat trusted me, against the advice of his comrades. I wonder whether, in his dying moments, he realised what a huge mistake he'd made.

Marat.speaker: FD9875B841C639C937411894C68D1042
Marat.statement: Marat was determined and ruthless. Unfortunately for him, so was Brencis.

Marat.speaker: 813B867B482D784ED625DBB27E0F0956
Marat.statement: Nothing brings you closer than facing mortal danger together. Marat and I became good friends...

Marat.speaker: 4994086240DCD33071B800A9118A0972
Marat.statement: Nothing brings you closer than facing mortal danger together. Marat and I became good friends...

Marat.speaker: F79ED43C40947577D04B1BA4AE6D0BC0
Marat.statement: With Catalin's return, the old order was restored, built on the sacrifice of the Manumits. A shame Marat never got to see it...

Marat.speaker: Coen
Marat.statement: The real Marat shines through sometimes, try as you may.

Crake.speaker: 100ED06F47B20FE7581E27BECD53F727
Crake.statement: I can't feel my arm. Crake, I can't feel it!

Crake.speaker: 608A1A7A48DF725EFE9E9B9B62089E2C
Crake.statement: 'Aurelius'… Crake, I think I’ve got something.

Crake.speaker: Mevasser
Crake.statement: Oh, they did... But, thank the Lord, not in the school. That's where Crake told his men to hide – without bothering to let me know beforehand.

Crake.speaker: Coen
Crake.statement: This might seem like an odd question, but do you think Crake is a good man?

Crake.speaker: 92D64985470982C5B17BDA9005E494D7
Crake.statement: Keep on fighting, then. Crake will notice, eventually.

Crake.speaker: Coen
Crake.statement: Keep on fighting. I'm sure Crake will notice – eventually.

Crake.speaker: OA105.Rebel
Crake.statement: Well, uh... Not yet! But the moment their noble leader, Crake, hears of my endeavours, he'll let me join the cause, I'm sure!

Crake.speaker: OB.DeadRebel
Crake.statement: I’m already dead. Do what you want. Just remember: Crake will do worse to you and yours.

Crake.speaker: cc_innkeeper2
Crake.statement: They say this Crake fellow isn't a mere human.

Crake.speaker: 1D8AC2E94663703375C378B7621E892B
Crake.statement: With time, I'll prove myself to Crake. He'll see that I've got balls – unlike Drogos.

Crake.speaker: Vladimir
Crake.statement: Talk to your father after Mass, convince him. Crake gave me the go-ahead – it's time to act.

Crake.speaker: Coen
Crake.statement: Listen, Sara. I need you to take me to Crake.

Crake.speaker: Sara
Crake.statement: Well, I'll tell you this – he's as safe as one can be in our ranks... But he won't help you get to Crake.

Crake.speaker: Sara
Crake.statement: [sigh] Fine. I'll let Crake decide what to do with you.

Crake.speaker: Q105_PostCommander
Crake.statement: But fear not. Crake will join the rest of the manumits soon enough... in our dungeon.

Crake.speaker: Q105_PostCommander
Crake.statement: Our knyaz has issued a warrant for an individual known as Crake. A very dangerous man.

Crake.speaker: Miller
Crake.statement: God, Crake will kill me. If the soldiers won't do it first...

Crake.speaker: Miller
Crake.statement: I... I think so. She’s a close confidant of Crake's.

Crake.speaker: Q105_Mert_Soul
Crake.statement: I... I don't know any Crake! I swear!

Crake.speaker: D33F6D4E41EA23F9BBA2D697C844117F
Crake.statement: You know, Crake… I’m starting to think you’re not as bad as you make yourself out to be.

Crake.speaker: 159814884A6D7052801B27A5063007F2
Crake.statement: I'm surprised Crake told you about it.

Crake.speaker: Q106_Random_Rebel4
Crake.statement: We still might. Depends on what Crake decides.

Crake.speaker: Drogos
Crake.statement: Crake told me already. I’ve sent someone to retrieve her body.

Crake.speaker: 3DA51CA24889947DC4861C8323573DFF
Crake.statement: This inscription... Crake has to see it.

Crake.speaker: 50DA2F2E4A95FA626EB6BAA3D7958B94
Crake.statement: Shit, even more blood... I hope it’s not all Crake’s.

Crake.speaker: 8FAD35064091078A1FF24F97677FF320
Crake.statement: That's done. I'd better keep looking for Crake.

Crake.speaker: 8717422A404604A58871E6B3F60E88E0
Crake.statement: This is Crake's sword. He must've dropped it in the struggle.

Crake.speaker: A9CA85DF46196019A0A9BF88F0E1174B
Crake.statement: It's not that, Crake. I just have to take care of something in Svartrau first.

Crake.speaker: 43B9DE5B420F30227DA25196E908EAD0
Crake.statement: My real name is Marat... if you prefer it to Crake.

Crake.speaker: 71BF6FBA4B02A027E3C4828A69026C78
Crake.statement: Crake let me join. He trusts me.

Crake.speaker: 0F5E956845DF495477A68DBF1B091F1A
Crake.statement: Exactly. I’m cheerful, Drogos is ill-tempered, Crake’s always on edge, and you... You seem kind, Coen. I like that about you.

Crake.speaker: 00ACE92D45FB45864F4A239EE38FCF5D
Crake.statement: Funny. Crake said the same thing when I joined.

Crake.speaker: Vladimir
Crake.statement: No. Crake... didn't like how I handled that.

Crake.speaker: Vladimir
Crake.statement: Only those in Crake's inner circle can.

Crake.speaker: 345D4549493496C06C26AAA37316AF8A
Crake.statement: [grunts] If you were looking for some bloody comforting, you should’ve gone to Crake, not me.

Crake.speaker: 0E3F6D72432A26C94FFFA2AD3042E1AF
Crake.statement: Listen to yourself, Crake. It's utter nonsense!

Crake.speaker: D6713CB64D6D177313E4A1BC694CC049
Crake.statement: Your pet seems lost, Crake. Fetch him, so we can move on.

Crake.speaker: 5831C587420F6887BD2298BC54B73A57
Crake.statement: I see. Another great example of your leadership... Crake.

Crake.speaker: 5281ED4F451E401C9432A7883E55A3DF
Crake.statement: Crake's gone, but you still have a chance... You can still avenge him.

Crake.speaker: 97210A674C45093BB3D5A59425EB5955
Crake.statement: You are my guests, after all... You and the elusive Crake.

Crake.speaker: E0BC1A1B4B18E72D1E329899AE2B4660
Crake.statement: Once we’re done here, Crake, I’ll bleed every last manumit dry.

Crake.speaker: C1A280BF4A371805D67EE8B8B65EE109
Crake.statement: And I'm the one who made it happen. I won Crake's favour... and now he's dead because of me.

Crake.speaker: 8AD450F84BEA1EDA92BACAA8C938BE73
Crake.statement: I know where the rebels are hiding. It's the weavers's guild building. Strike at the right time and you'll get Crake himself.

Crake.speaker: 9D1008684F23360C2660B4BEFCD9EEA1
Crake.statement: Coen! Yeah, Crake – sorry, Marat – said that he wanted to see Laslea, help [cough] help out with the rebuilding.

Crake.speaker: 1CB2F02B487FC90257491380963EB373
Crake.statement: Coen! Yeah, I decided to return home, finally. With Crake dead... well, there wasn't much for me to do amongst the Manumits.

Crake.speaker: B3E556BF43A8577078969697971A1DEE
Crake.statement: We were on the brink of winning this, Coen! Crake –

Crake.speaker: 7A4E125B4FE726A1C94BCCB90E97405F
Crake.statement: You sold us to Brencis. Crake and many good men and women died because of you.

Crake.speaker: Vladimir
Crake.statement: Don't look surprised. The fight's already started and Crake needs our help.

Crake.speaker: Vladimir
Crake.statement: There are men like us – in the capital. A man nicknamed Crake leads them.

Crake.speaker: Florin
Crake.statement: Their leader, Crake... He's the devil's spawn.

Crake.speaker: Drogos
Crake.statement: Crake's lot ain't easy. He does his best to keep a lid on things, but sometimes stuff boils over.

Crake.speaker: Drogos
Crake.statement: You and Crake should try it, too.

Crake.speaker: Marat
Crake.statement: Bah. All you see is Crake. Ruthless leader of the rebellion!

Crake.speaker: Vladimir
Crake.statement: Well, Crake does, of course. He keeps in touch with all the units, here and around the valley.

Drogos.speaker: Sara
Drogos.statement: I hate feeling like that... So, I’m going to ask Drogos to teach me swordplay.

Drogos.speaker: Marat
Drogos.statement: Ah, right. That. After reconsidering... I decided Drogos would handle it.

Drogos.speaker: Marat
Drogos.statement: I can’t trust him anymore. I’ll instruct Drogos to send him on a one-way trip to the countryside.

Drogos.speaker: Marat
Drogos.statement: I'll have Drogos cut out his tongue.

Drogos.speaker: Marat
Drogos.statement: You know, before Brencis, Drogos served knyaz Skender. He was one of his best soldiers.

Drogos.speaker: Coen
Drogos.statement: Go to the weavers's guild – and ask for Drogos. Tell him I sent you.

Drogos.speaker: A3938EF844401AAE1567D7900E4A158C
Drogos.statement: And yet, Drogos just drags his feet—reins us in.

Drogos.speaker: 9DCE8D134471FC0A68BBA0B53F38B61B
Drogos.statement: So you listen to Drogos. And to me, for that matter.

Drogos.speaker: 1D8AC2E94663703375C378B7621E892B
Drogos.statement: With time, I'll prove myself to Crake. He'll see that I've got balls – unlike Drogos.

Drogos.speaker: DD08E2484EEF04484483FC80423190B0
Drogos.statement: Yeah, I  guess... I guess you're right. [sigh] And who knows, maybe Drogos is, too.

Drogos.speaker: Marat
Drogos.statement: Fair enough... suppose I was too hasty in sending Drogos away.

Drogos.speaker: Coen
Drogos.statement: I didn't know Drogos was capable of joking.

Drogos.speaker: Marat
Drogos.statement: I ordered them to scatter. Drogos should know – Ah! Speak of the devil.

Drogos.speaker: Q106_Random_Rebel3
Drogos.statement: Not bad... but you’re leaving yourself too open. Drogos would have smacked you for that.

Drogos.speaker: Q106_Random_Rebel4
Drogos.statement: Well, I admit… it would be nice to see Drogos trashed. For a change.

Drogos.speaker: Coen
Drogos.statement: I hate to say it, Drogos... but you were right about me after all.

Drogos.speaker: 50EB4AA6418C731BEB3BF68FF8F05F12
Drogos.statement: Yeah, no worries... I've been worse. Drogos will patch me up, and I’ll be as good as new in a few days.

Drogos.speaker: 657F6E1D4CA99258C0D6DBA5E04527E0
Drogos.statement: I hate to say it, Drogos... but you were right about me after all.

Drogos.speaker: 0F5E956845DF495477A68DBF1B091F1A
Drogos.statement: Exactly. I’m cheerful, Drogos is ill-tempered, Crake’s always on edge, and you... You seem kind, Coen. I like that about you.

Drogos.speaker: 167B66A54A855BAC6715FEA328BD73CD
Drogos.statement: You’re awfully cheerful compared to the others... Especially Drogos.

Drogos.speaker: 534862184D329295787E04A439FCD6B2
Drogos.statement: One of Catalin's commanders, alongside Drogos, will lead a frontal assault on the castle. Meanwhile, our group will slip past enemy lines.

Drogos.speaker: 16BD52514B45FD598412A9B72CCD94E1
Drogos.statement: Aye. Drogos told me to protect our backs, hold my position no matter what... So I just watched them getting slaughtered.

Drogos.speaker: Marat
Drogos.statement: My father. Drogos has put the pieces together, too, by now.

Drogos.speaker: Coen
Drogos.statement: Enjoy your victory, Drogos. Next time I won't be pulling my punches.

Catalin.speaker: Ambrus
Catalin.statement: Is it just me, or is this Catalin utterly unbearable?

Catalin.speaker: peasant.male06
Catalin.statement: Of course not! But Catalin is no better than his old man. If folks are to die, it should be for someone much more worthy.

Catalin.speaker: Lacra
Catalin.statement: Hah. I'm starting to like this Catalin fellow.

Catalin.speaker: Marat
Catalin.statement: Catalin is at the border. He needs our help to break through the Eastridge Outpost.

Catalin.speaker: Coen
Catalin.statement: Catalin's as bad as the vrakhiri.

Catalin.speaker: Marat
Catalin.statement: Glad you see it that way. Some people – they don't look fondly on Catalin's return.

Catalin.speaker: Coen
Catalin.statement: Guess you're right. Catalin's better than Brencis.

Catalin.speaker: Marat
Catalin.statement: Knyaz Catalin is near, just beyond the mountains. We're in contact. Soon, he'll march in here with an army.

Catalin.speaker: Marat
Catalin.statement: Not quite yet. Catalin's forces need a few more days to reach the valley's edge. Until then, you're free to do whatever you wish.

Catalin.speaker: Coen
Catalin.statement: Please – let's work with Catalin, if we must, but if there's any way to keep him away from the throne –

Catalin.speaker: Marat
Catalin.statement: While they're focused on us, Catalin strikes from the other side. Once he’s through, we push forward and make our way to the castle.

Catalin.speaker: Coen
Catalin.statement: [sigh] Guess Catalin's marginally better than death...

Catalin.speaker: Coen
Catalin.statement: [sigh] Guess you're right... Even if Catalin isn't my dream sovereign, I sure prefer him to Brencis.

Catalin.speaker: OB109.Onlooker02
Catalin.statement: He was one of Skender's henchmen! Cavorted with young Catalin!

Catalin.speaker: Coen
Catalin.statement: And Catalin didn't like it.

Catalin.speaker: 5D4139244B0BAD40E10EFBA49FACDA15
Catalin.statement: And it looks like he was sent here by Catalin himself.

Catalin.speaker: D90259834D6B161598890490645E3FF0
Catalin.statement: I... I'm honoured, lord Catalin. But I'm not sure –

Catalin.speaker: 4283E57A498FA7621384E3BF014FF687
Catalin.statement: But worry not. With Catalin’s troops, the odds will even out.

Catalin.speaker: 05869F2343940F64366329A862A7ECA3
Catalin.statement: Someone needs to open the gate for Catalin’s troops!

Catalin.speaker: A482AB2946EF50ABD701FDA971331277
Catalin.statement: To the outer gate! Catalin needs our help!

Catalin.speaker: C7DF7D224AF03E0FCF2A809C2929578A
Catalin.statement: I'd use a different word... Raubritter... You see, Lord Catalin promised gold, and that was enough for most of them. Promised the city, too – free to loot, kill, take whatever they desired.

Catalin.speaker: 334757664F02A077663337A091E2CBCA
Catalin.statement: Indeed. I'm Edmund, supplier to Lord Catalin. I provide arms and provisions to those who serve his lordship’s cause.

Catalin.speaker: 853D3BCF4BFC58770F885D8C39B60403
Catalin.statement: Oh cheer up, mate. Lord Catalin promised us a lot of loot and fun at the castle.

Catalin.speaker: 534862184D329295787E04A439FCD6B2
Catalin.statement: One of Catalin's commanders, alongside Drogos, will lead a frontal assault on the castle. Meanwhile, our group will slip past enemy lines.

Catalin.speaker: C1E5FB9446DE2C8553120BB32E183D0E
Catalin.statement: There's a secret passage Catalin used to flee from the castle two years ago. We're going to take it to get in.

Catalin.speaker: A29BD33E4014C7BDD2613DAB46FB4AD8
Catalin.statement: Well, I'd imagined Lord Catalin, with all his pride and nobility, would raise a proper army. Not a ragtag bunch of coin-hungry cutthroats.

Catalin.speaker: 4367FBD64B15E940C8B627985C22EFE0
Catalin.statement: Catalin’s a dick. A dangerous one, at that.

Catalin.speaker: 2A776C9B424186C9697CCABA91D38830
Catalin.statement: Fuck. I warned Catalin this could happen. I bloody warned him.

Catalin.speaker: 5ECBAF9C4FEF4A645D6C9B8647EBF1C0
Catalin.statement: Aye, no warmth here. No comfort, just shadows and stone. No wonder Catalin turned out the way he did...

Catalin.speaker: 870C0B4A41B022C794F598BE0E12EEC9
Catalin.statement: Not sure how much time we've lost... But I hope Catalin and my men haven’t gone too far.

Catalin.speaker: BB9FBC784AFFBE9447EBC5AF5E43A14A
Catalin.statement: Ugh, Catalin's men, they ordered us to take the arsenal. Frontal attack.

Catalin.speaker: 5853633743A50418C24679A0E777E3DD
Catalin.statement: We'll never bend the knee to Catalin!

Catalin.speaker: B45DE281459D2509DB9210B20C76AF5D
Catalin.statement: Knyaz Catalin wants someone to eradicate them.

Catalin.speaker: 478E56EC4806B9572B07828683E0144A
Catalin.statement: Brencis is dead, Catalin is dead... Before long, people will start fighting over who'll be the next ruler.

Catalin.speaker: 096309C246D4D66751C4A5B5917FFFEE
Catalin.statement: Knyaz Catalin will probably help a bit, I reckon. But he's got quite a lot to do.

Catalin.speaker: ACFE9EE6439EA6F88C1307B792D32267
Catalin.statement: One of the first orders Catalin issued as the newly installed knyaz of Vale Sangora was to burn Florin at the stake.

Catalin.speaker: AD04F9C34D58A69DEC97619F4E00FC3F
Catalin.statement: Catalin didn't trust his own subjects and composed his army of foreign mercenaries. They didn't care much for Vale Sangora...

Catalin.speaker: E18565234BDC324BC6939896B9969704
Catalin.statement: Catalin was determined to stamp out all monsters from the valley. And, with Marat's help, he succeeded.

Catalin.speaker: EA5EFEDA4A35268C69281DA5C19CDAD0
Catalin.statement: Marat got what he wanted – he became Catalin's right hand man. And as such, he enforced his policies with ruthless efficiency...

Catalin.speaker: 148C549949AF949D5D0540B18C8D1D9B
Catalin.statement: Brencis was gone... But so was Catalin. With his death, Vale Sangora faced an uncertain future.

Catalin.speaker: F79ED43C40947577D04B1BA4AE6D0BC0
Catalin.statement: With Catalin's return, the old order was restored, built on the sacrifice of the Manumits. A shame Marat never got to see it...

Catalin.speaker: 6EBEA34A475B1825576315A1104F0920
Catalin.statement: With Catalin's return, the old order was restored... For better or for worse.

Catalin.speaker: Marat
Catalin.statement: Glad you see it that way. Some people - they don't take kindly to Catalin's return.

Catalin.speaker: Coen
Catalin.statement: Please - let's work with Catalin, if we have to, but if there's any way to keep him away from the throne...

Catalin.speaker: Marat
Catalin.statement: We help Knyaz Catalin cross the mountains – and storm Greifberg. Just like we discussed.

Catalin.speaker: Coen
Catalin.statement: [sighs] Guess you're right... Even if Catalin isn't my dream sovereign, I sure prefer him to Brencis.

Catalin.speaker: Brencis
Catalin.statement: A rebellion is brewing. Skender's exiled son, Catalin, is behind it.

Catalin.speaker: F93A20384A61C3AA64E92EB1899B8330
Catalin.statement: Knyaz Skender's firstborn, Catalin... Folk say he died in exile.

Pieter.speaker: Brencis
Pieter.statement: Poor Pieter... Cried like a little boy when I slit his throat.

Pieter.speaker: DB5489BD4A7EFABC49CA87ADBCA408A2
Pieter.statement: May Heaven bless you, Coen, son of Pieter.

Pieter.speaker: Vladimir
Pieter.statement: Good. Means Pieter could've hidden somewhere.

Pieter.speaker: Vladimir
Pieter.statement: Pieter's tough as nails. He'll be fine.

Pieter.speaker: Vladimir
Pieter.statement: He's alive. Maybe Pieter's somewhere nearby too.

Pieter.speaker: Vladimir
Pieter.statement: I've got a feeling Pieter's just around the corner.

Pieter.speaker: Vladimir
Pieter.statement: So I need an answer from Pieter – and I need it soon.

Pieter.speaker: Atanas
Pieter.statement: Ah, Coen. Pieter must be proud to have a son like you!

Pieter.speaker: Miller
Pieter.statement: You have such a kind heart... Pieter must be proud to have a son like you. I know we would be, if you were our own.

Pieter.speaker: Coen
Pieter.statement: Calm down, Mert. It's Coen, Pieter's son.

Pieter.speaker: Coen
Pieter.statement: It's Coen. Pieter's son.

Pieter.speaker: Coen
Pieter.statement: I took part in the attack on the mines near Laslea. With my father, Pieter. And Vladimir. You must know him.

Pieter.speaker: 301.necrospeak_corpse_05
Pieter.statement: Take Pieter and his family! Never mind the others!

Pieter.speaker: F9D7602E4D51F65D298FA593A3B70DE1
Pieter.statement: Ah! Good to see you again, Coen, son of Pieter.

Pieter.speaker: Gavril
Pieter.statement: Ah, knew I could count on you. Old Pieter raised you well.

Pieter.speaker: Esme
Pieter.statement: My children – Pieter – I can't take this –

Pieter.speaker: SQ711.Echo_Priest
Pieter.statement: ...Pieter and Esme. But not all is lost. No, God Almighty, in his mercy, has granted a small miracle.

Pieter.speaker: SQ711.Echo_Priest
Pieter.statement: ...breaking the hearts of his parents. Pieter and... And his wife...

Pieter.speaker: SQ711.Echo_Priest
Pieter.statement: ...to mourn the passing of young Alin. He departed this world too early, breaking the hearts of his parents, Pieter and... and...

Pieter.speaker: Coen
Pieter.statement: Alright, you got me. I am Pieter's son.

Pieter.speaker: Coen
Pieter.statement: Alright, you've got me. I am Pieter's son.

Pieter.speaker: Coen
Pieter.statement: No, sorry. I don’t know any Pieter.

Pieter.speaker: Maragir_Food
Pieter.statement: Oh, quit the act. You're Coen! Pieter's son!

Pieter.speaker: SQ719.Volk
Pieter.statement: Let’s drink to the memory of your father. Pieter, you old swine, may you rest in peace.

Pieter.speaker: SQ719.Volk
Pieter.statement: Pieter lay sprawled on the ground, covered in blood. I was ready to finish him off, but then he spat out a tooth and said 'Bet the soup's even colder now'.

Pieter.speaker: SQ719.Volk
Pieter.statement: Seems like Pieter was one secretive motherfucker!

Pieter.speaker: SQ719.Volk
Pieter.statement: Till the very end! But Pieter... He's always been different. Quiet, brooding... Bah! What does it matter now, anyway.

Pieter.speaker: SQ719.Volk
Pieter.statement: Before he knows it, he's on his knees, blood trickling down his split forehead. 'Spare me!', he squeals. 'Don't burden your conscience!'. And Pieter shoots back, 'You're right. Your horse can do the dirty work.'

Pieter.speaker: SQ719.Volk
Pieter.statement: Ah! Yes! The two brothers got drunk early and went to bed, snoring like red-haired swine. So Pieter came up with an idea.

Pieter.speaker: SQ719.Volk
Pieter.statement: Ha! Who would've thought Pieter would turn out to be such a hypocrite! Denying his son what he himself enjoyed.

Pieter.speaker: SQ719.Volk
Pieter.statement: Pieter and I were lending our swords to the French army. We killed over three thousand rebels, and lost just seventeen of our knights!

Pieter.speaker: Coen
Pieter.statement: Never seen it. Or anything Pieter could've bought with it.

Pieter.speaker: brencis_soldier.male10
Pieter.statement: I recognise you! You're Coen, son of Pieter!

Lacra.speaker: Isbrand
Lacra.statement: I should’ve killed you back then. Lacra was right.

Lacra.speaker: FE5BE30647C4780181062490A0D46E32
Lacra.statement: Ah, this 'Pale Lady' must be Lacra. Exactly what I’d expect her to do with a creepy stalker.

Lacra.speaker: Coen
Lacra.statement: It seems Lacra's actions haven't gone unnoticed.

Lacra.speaker: Coen
Lacra.statement: Lacra, calm down. We're going into their territory to ask for their help. It's fine.

Lacra.speaker: 1976148B4E4C02E4CE60D89BE1775C8E
Lacra.statement: You're right, Lacra. I've had it, too.

Lacra.speaker: A7F7A0E4439F53881E61FA9FE5940D42
Lacra.statement: You're right, Lacra. I've had it, too.

Lacra.speaker: F297B367420E2E1911CB479FC5A7A331
Lacra.statement: You're right, Lacra. I've had it, too.

Lacra.speaker: Coen
Lacra.statement: You're right, Lacra. I've tried, and I've had it, too. Let's do it your way.

Lacra.speaker: Coen
Lacra.statement: I invite you in, Lacra. For better or worse, I can't leave you here.

Lacra.speaker: Coen
Lacra.statement: You are blind, Lacra. You are a monster. And the fact that you don't realise it, well...

Lacra.speaker: Coen
Lacra.statement: I can do it, Lacra. I'll invite him in. You don't have to.

Lacra.speaker: Isbrand
Lacra.statement: I was a fool. I was. You have the right – Lacra. Every right to-to – refuse me. But don't. I meant – I didn't mean – I was –

Lacra.speaker: Isbrand
Lacra.statement: I'm sorry, Lacra. I'm... please... please, don't leave me...

Lacra.speaker: Coen
Lacra.statement: You should do it, Lacra. You've known him. It makes more sense.

Lacra.speaker: A4304E5E49300EA5F34200877F5355A9
Lacra.statement: Lacra was your daughter.

Lacra.speaker: Coen
Lacra.statement: Lacra was your daughter. And you–

Lacra.speaker: Coen
Lacra.statement: If this – this thing harms them, mangles them like that, Lacra, I swear –

Lacra.speaker: Coen
Lacra.statement: They'd better be here, Lacra. They'd better be alive.

Lacra.speaker: Coen
Lacra.statement: Lacra. This is Lunka's toy. She always has it on her.

Lacra.speaker: Xanthe
Lacra.statement: I wish you luck, Coen. As for you, Lacra, I hope your superiors have understanding for what you've done.

Lacra.speaker: Brencis
Lacra.statement: Ah, Lacra. Always ready to pounce. Always up for a fight.

Lacra.speaker: 3E426F854640BD0238B5588FCCF32419
Lacra.statement: The memory Lacra and I saw... these must be the ruins.

Lacra.speaker: 2F1BA7A544FDE61984B7CC91AC1ABF6B
Lacra.statement: I can lead you to your sworn enemy - Lacra.

Lacra.speaker: B2B1037B4A7C9C8FBDCCB19287FF5117
Lacra.statement: I can lead you to your sworn enemy - Lacra.

Lacra.speaker: 17A7A5DD437EC6D490BA34A5D144F5A7
Lacra.statement: I killed Lacra.

Lacra.speaker: 5FE4757246354B054F0C738979C0BF6B
Lacra.statement: I killed Lacra.

Lacra.speaker: 40C099294717A3A4987177A191F68F40
Lacra.statement: I killed your sworn enemy – Lacra. She meant to attack you.

Lacra.speaker: 467499C742752EF6ECABBFAE8821778E
Lacra.statement: I met a vrakhir named Lacra. I know she means to kill you.

Lacra.speaker: 2224ABD84C02364B1EFAE9A6D2E8AB56
Lacra.statement: Together with Lacra, I slayed every last one of the treacherous kobolds of the Rockfalls range. But their caves weren't empty for long.

Lacra.speaker: 335E25EB426C5D01E43A7BBCE8E8EDD1
Lacra.statement: Always on the run from someone, always outwitting her pursuers. Lacra didn't mind the constant danger – she revelled in it.

Lacra.speaker: 2282A83C43FB16490C4B73837C6DCBBB
Lacra.statement: Lacra did not linger in Vale Sangora.

Lacra.speaker: B4740DE4493D9441322379A30CC28A01
Lacra.statement: Lacra did not linger in Vale Sangora. Having defeated Brencis with my help, she swiftly moved on to other tasks, travelled to other places.

Lacra.speaker: 030BF3014A066FC5170E08A77FAE9962
Lacra.statement: Lacra died as she lived – driven, determined, unflinching. I wish I could tell you these virtues were rewarded in the afterlife that awaited her.

Lacra.speaker: A0ECE4F243D53BCC10EDEF8D4882CABE
Lacra.statement: Lacra was arrogant enough to think she could take Brencis and his clique on her own, without my help.

Lacra.speaker: 88D18DF34260EE1377BFB08363D08A75
Lacra.statement: Lacra was my first guide. She taught me what I needed to know, helped me when I needed assistance.

Lacra.speaker: FE72ED1E4ABB7C358F2772ADCE3304BB
Lacra.statement: Lacra was my first guide. She taught me what I needed to know, helped me when I needed assistance.

Lacra.speaker: Coen
Lacra.statement: Lacra told me about you and your shop. She said you might be able to help me.

Lacra.speaker: Vicho
Lacra.statement: A vrakhiri named Lacra. Don't really know her that well, but she's no ally to Brencis, that's for certain.

Lacra.speaker: Coen
Lacra.statement: Look at these roots, Lacra - they're growing in, from the outside.

Lacra.speaker: Coen
Lacra.statement: I think of all of them constantly, Lacra. It used to be just him, but now...

Lacra.speaker: Coen
Lacra.statement: You really don't like Lacra.

Vicho.speaker: Coen
Vicho.statement: Blood vials... Vicho could make use of them.

Vicho.speaker: Coen
Vicho.statement: These would make a perfect gift for Vicho.

Vicho.speaker: Lacra
Vicho.statement: Goes by the name of Vicho. And far as I know, he's none too thrilled about the way things are either.

Vicho.speaker: 79394C47429BECA0F1F851B195C06A34
Vicho.statement: Few suspected Vicho's true nature. The townspeople knew him as a kind, gentle man... Who aged very well.

Vicho.speaker: 0F79D5B24571158BE579AC97D3EAD013
Vicho.statement: I was convinced I'd solved the murders of Vicho's friends, but I was wrong – and more people died as a result.

Vicho.speaker: D3C9E2CF40D23D105932DBB963D15541
Vicho.statement: Vicho tried his best to make up for his many sins. It'll take a long time. But then - he is immortal.

Vicho.speaker: B8EAFE8042B37738E2B267B59A8800C4
Vicho.statement: When Vicho learned he was the one behind the deaths of his friends, he was devastated, ready to end his own life.

Vicho.speaker: Coen
Vicho.statement: No... Vicho, I can't! I can't stop it!

Vicho.speaker: Coen
Vicho.statement: I'm not arguing with you, Vicho. But we must focus on the task at hand.

Vicho.speaker: Coen
Vicho.statement: Dammit. Vicho, what have you done...

Vicho.speaker: Coen
Vicho.statement: Farewell, Vicho. I'm... I'm sorry this is how it ends.

Vicho.speaker: Coen
Vicho.statement: I'm sorry, Vicho. There's no easy way to say it – the doctor didn't kill Devora and Eli.

Vicho.speaker: Coen
Vicho.statement: Vicho... the man is dead. So is everyone else on the farm.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: You’re a fool… Isbrand… A blind, fucking fool!

Isbrand.speaker: Coen
Isbrand.statement: He had lost his mind, not unlike Isbrand. He's at rest now.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: He turned me, made me join Isbrand's clique, brought me to Europe. And let's leave it at that for now.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: But better suffer now and get Isbrand's golden thoughts than suffer later to Brencis's enjoyment. Ugh, what a thought!

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: If he is – well, that just makes me more certain that Isbrand turned into a problem.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: If not, Isbrand will still be useful – he knows his offspring inside and out.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: If there's someone who knows how to sneak up on Brencis, it's Isbrand.

Isbrand.speaker: Coen
Isbrand.statement: Do you know where the vrakhir Isbrand is?

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: Indeed. He's quite useless. The Elder of his village is the one who knows where Isbrand is.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: Must've pissed someone off. I'd like to think it was Isbrand, but I have my doubts.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: That's Isbrand's armour. You won't see that sort of craftsmanship around here.

Isbrand.speaker: Matriarch
Isbrand.statement: Only then - you follow and I show Isbrand.

Isbrand.speaker: Matriarch
Isbrand.statement: Brencis carry Isbrand inside, make sure he live. Sire useful one day, he say. We block off cave.

Isbrand.speaker: Matriarch
Isbrand.statement: No. Brencis keep secret. But he insist Isbrand never go free. Fear in eyes.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: I know where they put Isbrand.

Isbrand.speaker: Coen
Isbrand.statement: You know where Isbrand is?

Isbrand.speaker: FC3D8E6044D9E833858F9796F70E2E94
Isbrand.statement: You know where Isbrand is?

Isbrand.speaker: Matriarch
Isbrand.statement: Cave... At village end.... Blocked, with rock. Isbrand inside. Kobolds inside. He feed.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: Oh, yes. And Isbrand – our grandfather, so to speak – I knew him, too. We used to be in one clique.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: What's important is that Isbrand is sane and reliable. He wouldn't stand for Brencis's plans.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: No. We dispatched it too easily. Isbrand would add a new painting to the walls with its guts.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: Whatever became of Isbrand, his arrival was a big event for the kobold hive.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: Isbrand's body could potentially recover, with time... Plenty of time.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: Once we drain him fully, Isbrand will pull us to him. To Anachora.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: So we must drain Isbrand and follow him there.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: I used to belong to Isbrand's clique – along with Brencis.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: Isbrand had to punish someone and he didn't want to punish his prodigy.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: Our sire roped me into something Isbrand didn't like and I was made the example of.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: I'm sorry, Isbrand. I... I thought I could do it, but I was wrong.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: Brencis roped me into it and Isbrand didn't want to harm, or worse – get rid of – his prodigy. So he made an example out of me.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: Isbrand hoped that'd be enough. That Brencis would learn to respect the limits, abide by his sire's word.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: Isbrand is nestled within you. It's worth keeping your, heh, inner eye out for anything strange.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: So much for the great Isbrand.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: Well, be it as it may, we've got our answers – and I'm not surprised Isbrand guided us to them.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: Bloodshed rarely facilitates a good conversation. But Isbrand would never let people know about vrakhiri. No matter the cost.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: In the end, Isbrand was the one who had to learn a lesson.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: Isbrand's memories will be around somewhere – but getting to them might prove tricky.

Isbrand.speaker: Lacra
Isbrand.statement: This... all of this, Coen, is the result of tragic mistakes, cursed decisions. Both Isbrand's and mine.

Isbrand.speaker: Coen
Isbrand.statement: Isbrand tried to stop Brencis but failed. As punishment, he was imprisoned in kobold caves. They... they fed on him.

Anca.speaker: EB9D4FEF41876BD1459CD08572A9A484
Anca.statement: Anca's hut is over that way...

Anca.speaker: 744F19C04C68EACE1D689A8EB86543A6
Anca.statement: They're full of various herbs. Anca used plants like these to make medicine.

Anca.speaker: A5A5F9854F3F96194FCF5993003FF566
Anca.statement: Anca seems more than capable. Or maybe someone in Svartrau... A medic, perhaps?

Anca.speaker: 073EEE804D743BEA395F2EB61188016E
Anca.statement: Anca seems more than capable. Or maybe the medic from the Silberstein quarter in Svartrau.

Anca.speaker: 78BCCA3E4C878A5F141A798EE6FBDFF9
Anca.statement: Anca would be proud of me now.

Anca.speaker: 0C43619E4748F2EBADE230B3B76BFCC5
Anca.statement: I guess Anca would be proud of me now.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: I have the herbs. Anca said they should help.

Anca.speaker: Pieter
Anca.statement: Take the money – whatever's left. For Anca. And grab your sword, too.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: Here are the herbs from Anca.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: Here. New blend. Anca said it should help.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: This is the inn Anca told me about... But she's not here yet. I'd better come round later, then.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: Done. Now Anca should be able to make it to the library.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: I'm in... But no way Anca can follow me this way.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: So many books... No way I find the right one without Anca's help.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: The relic's missing... The soldiers must've taken it after Anca concluded her ritual.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: The relic's neither at the sacristy nor here... The soldiers must've taken it after Anca concluded the ritual.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: Anca. This woman was no saint.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: Anca – you feel guilty, I get that, but –

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: No! Anca, I'm not joking. This thing – for all we know, it'd kill you.

Anca.speaker: 1CB1324649537EF51C57A68D212A62E7
Anca.statement: Yeah. Anca said his bone grew back crooked.

Anca.speaker: 9616EB914CECEB5D2E20D48D19FC374F
Anca.statement: Anca can't vouch for it. There's a real risk it'd do more harm than good. But there's no other way.

Anca.speaker: DAA589474644D6B176B4B0A3BB8F8A40
Anca.statement: I also brought the potion from Anca's.

Anca.speaker: 0F7A9A92485ED1658901B7B80D7A0FC3
Anca.statement: Anca was restless. Looking for ways to undo the past - to cheat Death itself.

Anca.speaker: 1633EB16455564728A7322863F9764B1
Anca.statement: Anca... It just wasn't meant to last, what we had. Alas.

Anca.speaker: 514EACEC4FFB3DFC725D62859FC59F45
Anca.statement: Anca... It just wasn't meant to last, what we had. Alas.

Anca.speaker: 4CA66FC145AB9F8843C0799D8A0E183F
Anca.statement: I didn't let Anca finish the ritual Leonica started. There were too many unknowns, too many risks.

Anca.speaker: D654354641F4B31A5795C18EE1C15B5D
Anca.statement: Time to see if Anca was able to brew the potion.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: Anca is just a friend.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: Hm. Anca once pointed out this herb to me, said never to eat its berries... 'Not lethal, but moderately toxic,' from what I remember.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: Anca... Oh, no... I should've – God!

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: Fresh air... So there's another way out. Anca will be pleased.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: Anca... Enough with the cautionary tales. Enough with caution!

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: Anca... The world is in chaos, our lives turned upside down.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: Please, Anca. You've got an amazing mind. Don't let it dissolve into nightmares and regrets.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: That's where we'll find the Font! Come, Anca. Follow me.

Anca.speaker: Coen
Anca.statement: There's something here, Anca! I'll be right back!

Yanna.speaker: Brencis
Yanna.statement: I enjoyed Yanna's blood the most, I think.

Yanna.speaker: Coen
Yanna.statement: Mirto, Lunka, Yanna – they must be worried sick.

Yanna.speaker: Pieter
Yanna.statement: Yanna. Take Mirto and Lunka to the river. Vladimir says the trout are back, see if you can catch any.

Yanna.speaker: DB2C0667402FECEF04B228851F909D60
Yanna.statement: Oh, stop it Yanna! You're not my mum!

Yanna.speaker: 40D77D864A98DC5D8FDD43B5E77A75F3
Yanna.statement: Yanna said that you're not staying in Laslea. She said that because Lunka –

Yanna.speaker: AC6F4C5F4360D9CD940FF992BC963EB1
Yanna.statement: Yanna. Ever the responsible one. I hope she started a family of her own. I hope it was happier than ours.

Yanna.speaker: Coen
Yanna.statement: I will take care of you. And Yanna.

Yanna.speaker: Coen
Yanna.statement: I've got three siblings. Yanna, Mirto, Lunka. And I will do anything, anything, to keep them safe.

Yanna.speaker: Coen
Yanna.statement: She's gone, but Lunka, Mirto and Yanna – I will save them.

Yanna.speaker: Coen
Yanna.statement: Heh. My sister, Yanna – she would love these crayfish.

Mirto.speaker: Coen
Mirto.statement: Mirto, Lunka, Yanna – they must be worried sick.

Mirto.speaker: Coen
Mirto.statement: Oh, God. Mirto, Yana, Lunka – There's no time.

Mirto.speaker: Yanna
Mirto.statement: Shush, Mirto. You'll make Lunka cry again.

Mirto.speaker: Pieter
Mirto.statement: Yanna. Take Mirto and Lunka to the river. Vladimir says the trout are back, see if you can catch any.

Mirto.speaker: Coen
Mirto.statement: Pretty little figurine... Dad made a similar one for Mirto.

Mirto.speaker: FD593FDF46B55B3A31144DA69F205860
Mirto.statement: God, you're right. For so long... you've been there for us. You took care of Mirto... Of Lunka.

Mirto.speaker: 6F5D3F13407A4EC3879B81A412722C82
Mirto.statement: Mirto... As stubborn as he was brave. I wonder what kind of man he grew up to be. Whether he remembered me.

Mirto.speaker: E60A621F4BCEC3229410888EBE468C44
Mirto.statement: Mirto's toy. Good to see he's still able to play like he used to.

Mirto.speaker: Coen
Mirto.statement: Yes. I started when I was a bit older than Mirto, did it for almost a decade.

Mirto.speaker: Coen
Mirto.statement: Maybe Lunka or Mirto will want to learn.

Mirto.speaker: Yanna
Mirto.statement: Oi! I've had it with you, Mirto. Not another word!

Mirto.speaker: Coen
Mirto.statement: I've got three siblings. Yanna, Mirto, Lunka. And I will do anything, anything, to keep them safe.

Mirto.speaker: Pieter
Mirto.statement: Well, yes. Lunka and Mirto asked for olatki to break the fast, and we're almost out of kindling.

Mirto.speaker: Coen
Mirto.statement: She's gone, but Lunka, Mirto and Yanna – I will save them.

Lunka.speaker: Coen
Lunka.statement: His father nearly killed me! And Lunka, too!

Lunka.speaker: Coen
Lunka.statement: Mirto, Lunka, Yanna – they must be worried sick.

Lunka.speaker: Coen
Lunka.statement: Oh, God. Mirto, Yana, Lunka – There's no time.

Lunka.speaker: Coen
Lunka.statement: Oh, God. My mother, Lunka – There's no time.

Lunka.speaker: Coen
Lunka.statement: I... I had that nightmare again. Lunka and me, getting turned.

Lunka.speaker: Yanna
Lunka.statement: Shush, Mirto. You'll make Lunka cry again.

Lunka.speaker: Pieter
Lunka.statement: Yanna. Take Mirto and Lunka to the river. Vladimir says the trout are back, see if you can catch any.

Lunka.speaker: Coen
Lunka.statement: Piece of cloth... From Lunka's dress. Maybe she tried to jump out, run away, but...

Lunka.speaker: Coen
Lunka.statement: This is Lunka's... Oh, God.

Lunka.speaker: Coen
Lunka.statement: Lacra. This is Lunka's toy. She always has it on her.

Lunka.speaker: Coen
Lunka.statement: This... this was Lunka's toy... She always had it on her.

Lunka.speaker: F5439F934FDB0385311990901256E8F4
Lunka.statement: I know this. It's Lunka's. Oh, God...

Lunka.speaker: FD593FDF46B55B3A31144DA69F205860
Lunka.statement: God, you're right. For so long... you've been there for us. You took care of Mirto... Of Lunka.

Lunka.speaker: 40D77D864A98DC5D8FDD43B5E77A75F3
Lunka.statement: Yanna said that you're not staying in Laslea. She said that because Lunka –

Lunka.speaker: 92C1BC194EF12390497E8689D2E0ECE6
Lunka.statement: And a fat lot of good it did. With Lunka -

Lunka.speaker: C5802B014495FFB229AA6F89DF97072A
Lunka.statement: Lunka... I'm so sorry. I should have been there to protect you.

Lunka.speaker: A2B250514DEDA9F47E5A6A89F9D95BC6
Lunka.statement: As for Lunka... My fate was intertwined with hers. For all eternity.

Lunka.speaker: 447B0ECB453D541A6972F9A92766F3D7
Lunka.statement: Only Lunka survived... To suffer for all eternity.

Lunka.speaker: Coen
Lunka.statement: But taking it out on us won't help anyone. Lunka, especially.

Lunka.speaker: Coen
Lunka.statement: Hey. I get it, Lunka, you love all the animals in the world, but –

Lunka.speaker: Coen
Lunka.statement: Maybe Lunka or Mirto will want to learn.

Lunka.speaker: Coen
Lunka.statement: I've got three siblings. Yanna, Mirto, Lunka. And I will do anything, anything, to keep them safe.

Lunka.speaker: Pieter
Lunka.statement: Lunka... she said that she got messages from you... delivered by fairies!

Lunka.speaker: Coen
Lunka.statement: She's gone, but Lunka, Mirto and Yanna – I will save them.

Lunka.speaker: Brencis
Lunka.statement: You mock me. But when Lunka was dying in your arms, didn't you beg for help?

Esme.speaker: Anca
Esme.statement: But Esme isn't sick. It's her mind that's ailing. So dark and troubled she won't even eat... And so she grows weaker.

Esme.speaker: Anca
Esme.statement: Esme... She's tangled up in her own, awful thoughts, unable to break free.

Esme.speaker: Pieter
Esme.statement: But since you took your sweet time coming home... Soon as we give Esme the herbs, we'll have to get ready for Mass.

Esme.speaker: Iorgu
Esme.statement: I'm sure Esme will be fine. Chin up!

Esme.speaker: EA1970DE4DDC0A167F9BE782F5AD1A57
Esme.statement: At least now she's with poor Esme. And with my Kvet.

Esme.speaker: SQ711.Echo_Priest
Esme.statement: ...Pieter and Esme. But not all is lost. No, God Almighty, in his mercy, has granted a small miracle.

Neberu.speaker: 09434A36433B32D28F13198FE6AAF1DF
Neberu.statement: My name is Neberu. We haven't met – I arrived in Vale Sangora only recently.

Neberu.speaker: B9B4E88246890FFF9393B695D8C3D1FC
Neberu.statement: My name is Neberu. We haven't met – I arrived in Vale Sangora only recently.

Sara.speaker: Marat
Sara.statement: Morale is up and down, I won't lie. The massacre of our scouts, news about the gargoyles, Sara’s death… it’s all weighed heavily on their hearts.

Sara.speaker: Marat
Sara.statement: Very well. I'll fetch Sara, and we'll set off after dark.

Sara.speaker: Coen
Sara.statement: Listen, Sara. I need you to take me to Crake.

Sara.speaker: Miller
Sara.statement: Coen, listen – you've got to help Sara, too.

Sara.speaker: Miller
Sara.statement: I... I thought I could do this. Now Sara's in danger, and I... I'm a traitor.

Sara.speaker: Miller
Sara.statement: I... I'll tell you what – there's this girl, Sara. You help her and me... And you'll reach them.

Sara.speaker: Miller
Sara.statement: Thank you, thank you... B-But wait! You've got to help Sara too!

Sara.speaker: Miller
Sara.statement: You – you've got to help me, Coen. And Sara, too. Please.

Sara.speaker: Coen
Sara.statement: I saved Sara at the rendezvous point.

Sara.speaker: 7932EA0F41B2891EB1F16ABB23EBDBC4
Sara.statement: I saved Sara at the rendezvous point.

Sara.speaker: 34366D074F8DEC87EC876A8904500101
Sara.statement: I bet Sara could drink us both under the table.

Sara.speaker: 2229CA7E43F4D88F11A0359184767D88
Sara.statement: I bet Sara could've drunk us both under the table. Laughing while she was at it.

Sara.speaker: 98A1E9FD4B8735EF4A923E932E8B2313
Sara.statement: I know Sara would have, without batting an eye. That's the real reason I brought her tonight – she understood these things.

Sara.speaker: 49BB7D9740661012C4778F961E5C4373
Sara.statement: [scoffs] You did have a choice. We could’ve still saved Sara!

Sara.speaker: F91B08C3485F7C3718CC6F96EA7E71CF
Sara.statement: It's Sara. She was crushed by debris.

Sara.speaker: Marat
Sara.statement: This is serious, Sara. We have to prepare.

Sara.speaker: FD0C6F6D4278B45EE408E1B9930A4586
Sara.statement: Sara was right. I do care about those I trust, and at this point... there's no denying I trust you.

Ascar.speaker: Coen
Ascar.statement: ...Ascar went about his day. Nothing overtly suspicious. But then, some soldiers beat him up.

Ascar.speaker: Coen
Ascar.statement: Some soldiers tried to rough Ascar up, but I dealt with them.

Ascar.speaker: Marat
Ascar.statement: There's a man in Tantari, a beekeeper by the name of Ascar. He's... of interest to us.

Ascar.speaker: SQ713_Village_woman
Ascar.statement: You work too hard, Ascar. You need a break.

Ascar.speaker: Coen
Ascar.statement: Can't let Ascar see me. Got to get behind this tree.

Ascar.speaker: Coen
Ascar.statement: That must be Ascar... But he's asleep.

Ascar.speaker: Coen
Ascar.statement: Ascar is your father, isn't he?

Ascar.speaker: Marat
Ascar.statement: Ascar's case is closed. There's nothing to add.

Aurelius.speaker: 608A1A7A48DF725EFE9E9B9B62089E2C
Aurelius.statement: 'Aurelius'… Crake, I think I’ve got something.

Aurelius.speaker: Coen
Aurelius.statement: Aurelius doesn’t matter anymore. I’d rather focus on attacking the castle.

Aurelius.speaker: Marat
Aurelius.statement: Guess at this point it wouldn't surprise me if you made Aurelius himself teach it to you.

Aurelius.speaker: Coen
Aurelius.statement: I did. The language matches. There are some notes in the margins, too. I’m pretty sure Aurelius wrote them.

Aurelius.speaker: Coen
Aurelius.statement: I haven’t had the pleasure of meeting Master Aurelius, but I did meet his apprentice…

Aurelius.speaker: Coen
Aurelius.statement: No, into his assistant. Aurelius stayed holed up in the chambers at the top of the tower.

Aurelius.speaker: Coen
Aurelius.statement: No. I had the displeasure of meeting his apprentice, but Aurelius never showed up, even during our fight.

Aurelius.speaker: Coen
Aurelius.statement: Oh, I did meet Master Aurelius – but I was the one teaching him a lesson. One he, regrettably, won’t recover from.

Aurelius.speaker: D4A9A37642DC750AE65A6B82AA23F9BC
Aurelius.statement: Master Aurelius! I need help with this one!

Aurelius.speaker: 731898F64F42E491332093B16A27265C
Aurelius.statement: Aurelius works for the knyaz. No doubt about it anymore.

Aurelius.speaker: Coen
Aurelius.statement: But Aurelius... He's still alive. Still here somewhere.

Pixies.speaker: Coen
Pixies.statement: All this just reeks of sanzhani. They're behind it, I'm sure.

Pixies.speaker: Coen
Pixies.statement: The sanzhani... They didn't want their forest cut down, it seems.

Pixies.speaker: Zdislav
Pixies.statement: Said he was taken by the forest spirits, the sanzhani – they raised him. Tiny creatures with wings.

Sanzhani Tsarina.speaker: D4216E3242A88E51BC5FD1837B3F3E2D
Sanzhani Tsarina.statement: I'll tell our tsarina of your deeds. She'll be pleased, I'm sure. But there's more.

Sanzhani Tsarina.speaker: 463C3B894B45012AEE43C7A05A25753E
Sanzhani Tsarina.statement: You've avenged my sisters. That's plenty. And I'll make sure our tsarina hears of it.
